exposure: support for institutional delivery by the husband
decision on place of delivery taken jointly by women and family members
decision on place of delivery taken by family members alone
complications during the most recent pregnancy/delivery
perception that skilled health workers are always available
birthing facility located within one hour's travelling distance
not knowing about the adequacy of physical facilities
cohort: Mothers who had given birth during a one-year period in six rural Village Development Committees of Chitwan district, Nepal.
finding: Socio-demographic, socio-cultural, and health service-related factors, including husband's support and family decision-making roles, significantly influenced the likelihood of institutional delivery.
cross-section timing: Mothers who had given birth during a one-year period prior to the study interview.
